jhmt-2020-tr2-01a.title: Negate then add
jhmt-2020-tr2-01a.body: To find $a-b$: construct $-b$ as in Example 1.2 (the second intersection of the line with the circle of radius $b$ about $0$; if $b=0$ there is nothing to do), then add $-b$ to $a$ as in Example 1.1. The result is $a+(-b)=a-b$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-01b.title: Similar triangles
jhmt-2020-tr2-01b.body: Draw a ray $l$ from $0$ not along $\mathcal R$. Draw the circle of radius $|b|$ about $0$ and let $C$ be its intersection with $l$. Join $1$ and $C$; call this segment $m$. Through $a$, construct the line parallel to $m$, and let $D$ be its intersection with $l$. Since $1C\parallel aD$, triangles $0,1,C$ and $0,a,D$ are similar, so $\frac{0D}{0C}=\frac{0a}{01}$, i.e. $0D=|a|\,|b|$. Transfer this length back to $\mathcal R$ with a circle about $0$, choosing the side of $0$ given by the signs of $a$ and $b$ (using Example 1.2 to negate if needed). This point is $ab$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-01c.title: Similar triangles
jhmt-2020-tr2-01c.body: Draw a ray $l$ from $0$ not along $\mathcal R$. Draw the circle of radius $1$ about $0$ and let $C$ be its intersection with $l$. Join $a$ and $C$; call this segment $m$. Through $1$, construct the line parallel to $m$, and let $D$ be its intersection with $l$. By similar triangles $0,a,C$ and $0,1,D$, $\frac{0D}{0C}=\frac{01}{0a}$, so $0D=\frac{1}{|a|}$. Transfer this length to $\mathcal R$ on the same side of $0$ as $a$. This point is $\frac1a$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-01d.title: Reciprocal then multiply
jhmt-2020-tr2-01d.body: To find $\frac ab$ with $b\ne0$: construct $\frac1b$ by part (c), then multiply $a$ by $\frac1b$ using part (b). The result is $a\cdot\frac1b=\frac ab$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-02.title: Similar right triangles
jhmt-2020-tr2-02.body:
Join $AD$ and $DB$. Since $AB$ is a diameter, $\angle ADB=90^\circ$ (Thales). In right triangle $APD$, $\angle DAP=90^\circ-\angle ADP$. Since $\angle ADP+\angle PDB=\angle ADB=90^\circ$, also $\angle PDB=90^\circ-\angle ADP$, so $\angle DAP=\angle PDB$. Both $\triangle APD$ and $\triangle DPB$ have a right angle at $P$, so they are similar (AA), with $A\leftrightarrow D$, $P\leftrightarrow P$, $D\leftrightarrow B$. Hence
$$\frac{AP}{PD}=\frac{PD}{PB}\implies PD^2=AP\cdot PB=a\cdot1=a,$$
and $\overline{PD}=\sqrt a$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-03a.title: Direct choice
jhmt-2020-tr2-03a.body: Take $\alpha=\beta=\sqrt2$, which is irrational. Then $\alpha^\beta=\sqrt2^{\sqrt2}$, which is rational by assumption, so the proposition holds.

jhmt-2020-tr2-03b.title: Raise to the power sqrt 2
jhmt-2020-tr2-03b.body:
Take $\alpha=\sqrt2^{\sqrt2}$, irrational by assumption, and $\beta=\sqrt2$, also irrational. Then
$$\alpha^\beta=\left(\sqrt2^{\sqrt2}\right)^{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2^{\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2}=\sqrt2^{\,2}=2,$$
which is rational. Together with part (a) and PEM (the number $\sqrt2^{\sqrt2}$ is either rational or irrational), the proposition is proved.

jhmt-2020-tr2-04a.title: Uniqueness in Axiom 2.1
jhmt-2020-tr2-04a.body: Define $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ by $f(d)=ad$. Since $ad=bd$ for every $d\in\mathcal D$, also $f(d)=bd$ for every $d$. So $f(d)=0+a\,d$ and $f(d)=0+b\,d$ are two expressions of the same function in the form of Axiom 2.1. The constants in that form are unique, so $a=b$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-04b.title: Contradiction with uniqueness
jhmt-2020-tr2-04b.body: Suppose $\mathcal D=\{0\}$. Consider $f(d)=0+0\cdot d$ and $g(d)=0+1\cdot d$ on $\mathcal D$. The only element of $\mathcal D$ is $0$, and $f(0)=0=g(0)$, so $f$ and $g$ are the same function. By the uniqueness in Axiom 2.1 (equivalently, part (a) with $a=0$, $b=1$), $0=1$. This is absurd, since $0$ and $1$ are different marked points. Hence $\mathcal D\ne\{0\}$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-04c.title: Compute the square
jhmt-2020-tr2-04c.body: Let $d_1,d_2\in\mathcal D$. By associativity and commutativity of multiplication, $(d_1d_2)^2=d_1^2\,d_2^2=0\cdot0=0$. So $d_1d_2\in\mathcal D$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-05a.title: Use the definition
jhmt-2020-tr2-05a.body: For every $d\in\mathcal D$, $f_5(d)=f(5+d)=8=8+0\cdot d$. By the uniqueness in Axiom 2.1, the coefficient of $d$ is the derivative, so $f'(5)=\boxed{0}$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-05b.title: Use the definition
jhmt-2020-tr2-05b.body:
For $d\in\mathcal D$,
$$(2+d)\left(\frac12-\frac d4\right)=1+\frac d2-\frac d2-\frac{d^2}{4}=1,$$
so $2+d$ is invertible and $f_2(d)=\frac{1}{2+d}=\frac12-\frac14d$. (Equivalently, $\frac{1}{2+d}=\frac{2-d}{4-d^2}=\frac{2-d}{4}$.) The coefficient of $d$ is the derivative: $f'(2)=\boxed{-\frac14}$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-06.title: Expand
jhmt-2020-tr2-06.body:
For $d\in\mathcal D$, $d^2=0$ and $d^3=d\cdot d^2=0$, so
$$f(x+d)=(x^3+3x^2d+3xd^2+d^3)-(x+d)+1=(x^3-x+1)+d\,(3x^2-1).$$
By the definition of the derivative function, $f'(x)=3x^2-1$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-07a.title: Constant multiple
jhmt-2020-tr2-07a.body: For $d\in\mathcal D$, $(cf)(x+d)=c\,f(x+d)=c\,(f(x)+d\,f'(x))=(cf)(x)+d\cdot c\,f'(x)$. (By Axiom 2.1, if $F(x+d)=F(x)+c\,d$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$, then $F'(x)=c$.) Hence $(cf)'(x)=c\,f'(x)$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-07b.title: Sum rule
jhmt-2020-tr2-07b.body:
For $d\in\mathcal D$,
$$(f+g)(x+d)=f(x+d)+g(x+d)=f(x)+d\,f'(x)+g(x)+d\,g'(x)=(f+g)(x)+d\,(f'(x)+g'(x)).$$
(By Axiom 2.1, if $F(x+d)=F(x)+c\,d$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$, then $F'(x)=c$.) Hence $(f+g)'=f'+g'$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-07c.title: Product rule
jhmt-2020-tr2-07c.body:
For $d\in\mathcal D$,
$$(fg)(x+d)=(f(x)+d\,f'(x))(g(x)+d\,g'(x))=f(x)g(x)+d\,(f(x)g'(x)+f'(x)g(x))+d^2f'(x)g'(x).$$
Since $d^2=0$, this is $(fg)(x)+d\,(f(x)g'(x)+f'(x)g(x))$. (By Axiom 2.1, if $F(x+d)=F(x)+c\,d$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$, then $F'(x)=c$.) Hence $(fg)'=fg'+f'g$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-07d.title: Quotient rule
jhmt-2020-tr2-07d.body:
Fix $x$ with $g(x)\ne0$ and write $f,f',g,g'$ for their values at $x$. For $d\in\mathcal D$, $(g+dg')(g-dg')=g^2-d^2g'^2=g^2$, so $g(x+d)=g+dg'$ is invertible with inverse $\frac{g-dg'}{g^2}$. Hence
$$\frac fg(x+d)=\frac{f+df'}{g+dg'}=\frac{(f+df')(g-dg')}{g^2}=\frac{fg+d\,(gf'-fg')-d^2f'g'}{g^2}=\frac fg+d\cdot\frac{gf'-fg'}{g^2}.$$
(By Axiom 2.1, if $F(x+d)=F(x)+c\,d$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$, then $F'(x)=c$.) Hence $(f/g)'=(gf'-fg')/g^2$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-07e.title: Chain rule
jhmt-2020-tr2-07e.body:
Fix $x$ and let $d\in\mathcal D$. Then $g(x+d)=g(x)+\delta$ with $\delta=d\,g'(x)$, and $\delta^2=d^2g'(x)^2=0$, so $\delta\in\mathcal D$. Applying the definition of $f'$ at the point $g(x)$ with the infinitesimal $\delta$:
$$(f\circ g)(x+d)=f(g(x)+\delta)=f(g(x))+\delta\,f'(g(x))=(f\circ g)(x)+d\cdot g'(x)\,f'(g(x)).$$
(By Axiom 2.1, if $F(x+d)=F(x)+c\,d$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$, then $F'(x)=c$.) Hence $(f\circ g)'(x)=f'(g(x))\cdot g'(x)$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-08a.title: Half-angle
jhmt-2020-tr2-08a.body:
From $\sin^2d+\cos^2d=1$ and $\sin^2d=d^2=0$ we get $\cos^2d=1$. To pin down the sign without excluded middle, let $e=\frac d2$; then $e^2=\frac{d^2}{4}=0$, so $e\in\mathcal D$ and $\sin e=e$. By the addition formula for cosine and $\sin^2e+\cos^2e=1$,
$$\cos d=\cos(e+e)=\cos^2e-\sin^2e=(1-\sin^2e)-\sin^2e=1-2e^2=1.$$
So $\cos d=1$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-08b.title: Addition formula
jhmt-2020-tr2-08b.body:
For $d\in\mathcal D$, using $\cos d=1$ and $\sin d=d$:
$$\sin(x+d)=\sin x\cos d+\cos x\sin d=\sin x+d\cos x.$$
By the definition of the derivative function, $(\sin x)'=\cos x$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-08c.title: Addition formula
jhmt-2020-tr2-08c.body:
For $d\in\mathcal D$, using $\cos d=1$ and $\sin d=d$:
$$\cos(x+d)=\cos x\cos d-\sin x\sin d=\cos x+d\,(-\sin x).$$
By the definition of the derivative function, $(\cos x)'=-\sin x$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-09a.title: Area of triangle OPQ
jhmt-2020-tr2-09a.body:
Write $r=r(t_0)$, $r'=r'(t_0)$, $\theta'=\theta'(t_0)$. By the axiom, during the infinitesimal time $d$ the particle moves along the straight segment $PQ$, so the region swept by the cord is triangle $OPQ$. Here $OP=r$, $OQ=r(t_0+d)=r+d\,r'$, and $\angle POQ=\theta(t_0+d)-\theta(t_0)=d\,\theta'$. Since $(d\theta')^2=d^2\theta'^2=0$, $d\theta'\in\mathcal D$ and $\sin(d\theta')=d\theta'$. Therefore
$$[OPQ]=\frac12\,OP\cdot OQ\cdot\sin\angle POQ=\frac12\,r\,(r+dr')\,d\theta'=\frac12\,d\,r^2\theta'+\frac12\,d^2\,rr'\theta'=\frac12\,d\,r^2(t_0)\,\theta'(t_0).$$

jhmt-2020-tr2-09b.title: Compare with the definition
jhmt-2020-tr2-09b.body:
For every $d\in\mathcal D$, $A(t_0+d)-A(t_0)$ is the area swept between times $t_0$ and $t_0+d$, which by part (a) is $\frac12dr^2(t_0)\theta'(t_0)$. So
$$A(t_0+d)=A(t_0)+d\cdot\tfrac12r^2(t_0)\theta'(t_0)\quad\text{for all }d\in\mathcal D.$$
By definition also $A(t_0+d)=A(t_0)+d\,A'(t_0)$, so $d\,A'(t_0)=d\cdot\frac12r^2(t_0)\theta'(t_0)$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$. By Problem 4(a), $A'(t_0)=\frac12r^2(t_0)\theta'(t_0)$.

jhmt-2020-tr2-09c.title: Product and chain rules
jhmt-2020-tr2-09c.body:
By the product rule and the chain rule with $(\cos)'=-\sin$, $(\sin)'=\cos$:
$$x'=(r\cos\theta)'=r'\cos\theta+r\cdot(-\sin\theta)\,\theta'=r'\cos\theta-r\theta'\sin\theta,$$
$$y'=(r\sin\theta)'=r'\sin\theta+r\cos\theta\,\theta'=r'\sin\theta+r\theta'\cos\theta.$$

jhmt-2020-tr2-09d.title: Differentiate 2A'
jhmt-2020-tr2-09d.body:
Using part (c),
$$xy'-yx'=r\cos\theta\,(r'\sin\theta+r\theta'\cos\theta)-r\sin\theta\,(r'\cos\theta-r\theta'\sin\theta)=r^2\theta'(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)=r^2\theta'=2A'.$$
Differentiating with the sum, product and constant-multiple rules,
$$2A''=(x'y'+xy'')-(y'x'+yx'')=xy''-yx''=0$$
by Newton's law. Hence $A''=0$.
